howto.name: Choose a direction
howto.text: Pick YAML to TOML, the default, or TOML to YAML with the switch above the editor. The text stays when you switch, so paste input in the new source format; the YAML sample read as TOML shows an error.

howto.name: Paste your config
howto.text: Paste the config text into the input box; there is no file upload. Nested mappings and tables, strings, numbers, true and false, and arrays of plain values are converted, and comments are dropped.

howto.name: Read the converted config
howto.text: The Converted config panel updates as you type. YAML to TOML writes tables with dotted headers such as [server.tls] and inline arrays; TOML to YAML writes nested mappings indented two spaces, - lists and double-quoted strings.

howto.name: Fix any error shown
howto.text: If the input cannot be converted, a red message starting with Error: replaces the output and Copy is disabled. Indentation and key errors in YAML name the line, for example Error: Use spaces for indentation on line 2.

howto.name: Copy the converted config
howto.text: Click Copy to put the result on your clipboard, then paste it into your file. There is no download button.

faq.q: What does a YAML to TOML conversion look like?
faq.a: The sample YAML has app with name: privatools and port: 8000, and features with localOnly: true and retries: 3. With / marking a line break it becomes [app] / name = "privatools" / port = 8000, a blank line, then [features] / localOnly = true / retries = 3.

faq.q: What does TOML to YAML produce?
faq.a: [server] followed by port = 8080 and tags = ["a", "b"] becomes server: / port: 8080 / tags: / - "a" / - "b" (/ marks a line break), with port and tags indented two spaces and the list items four. Empty TOML input converts to {}.

Sometimes. Within each TOML table, plain keys come first and sub-tables after, so a YAML server block that lists tls: before host and port produces [server] with host and port, then [server.tls]. Keys that are whole numbers, such as 404, move ahead of the other keys in ascending order, in both directions.

faq.q: Which YAML features are not supported?
faq.a: Anchors, aliases, tags and | or > multiline strings (Error: Anchors, tags and multiline scalar syntax are not supported in this editor.), more than one document, tab indentation, << merge keys and duplicate keys. Inline {...} objects must be JSON with quoted keys. A list of mappings, such as jobs with - name: build, stops with Error: Arrays of objects require TOML array tables, which this editor does not support. Empty input, a bare list or a single value shows Error: TOML needs a mapping at the document root.

faq.q: Which TOML features are not supported?
faq.a: Array tables such as [[bin]] and quoted table names (Error: Use simple table names. Array tables and quoted table paths are not supported.), dotted keys like a.b = 1, arrays or strings spread over several lines, and inline tables such as { x = 1 } unless written as JSON. Unquoted text values, including numbers written as 1_000, 0xFF or inf, stop with an error such as Error: Quote the string value for n.

faq.q: Can values change on the way through?
faq.a: Unquoted numbers are read as numbers, so 01234 becomes 1234 and 1.0 becomes 1; quote them to keep the text. In YAML only lowercase true and false are booleans, so yes, on and True become strings. Dates such as 2024-05-01 become quoted strings. Whole numbers beyond JavaScript's safe range must be quoted, and YAML null, ~ or an empty value stops with Error: TOML has no null value. Remove or replace null values before converting.
No. Comments are removed in both directions. A # only starts a comment at the start of a line or after whitespace, outside quotes, so http://example.com/#top keeps its fragment.
No. Parsing and writing run in your browser; the tool makes no network request with your config and does not save it in browser storage.
